coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 only (140 bpm ceiling), on flat or rolling terrain. You ran 14 mi with 2,388 ft vert yesterday at 122 avg HR—solid work—but your recovery score is 65/100 and sleep was only 6h. Monday in taper is your reset; no intensity, no vert. This is a shakeout to flush legs and keep the aerobic engine ticking. Aim for conversational effort; if your watch shows a spike above 145 bpm, dial it back immediately.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Prioritize carbs today: 6–7 g/kg of body weight (assume ~75 kg, so 450–525g total). Your short sleep signals elevated cortisol and glycogen depletion risk. Front-load breakfast with oats, fruit, and eggs; add a rice or pasta-based lunch and dinner. During the easy run, sip 200–300 cal/hr (sports drink or gel + water) to top off tanks without stressing digestion. This isn't race fuel practice; it's recovery fuel.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is the bottleneck right now. You averaged 8.27h over 30 days but hit only 6h last night—that's a 2+ hour deficit. Tonight, non-negotiable: 10-hour window in bed (no compromise on travel schedule), blackout blinds, phone off by 21:30. Cold shower post-run to lower core temp. Resting HR is already solid at 62 bpm, but poor sleep will spike it back toward 70+. The Julian Alps requires full nervous system recovery; you can't afford sleep debt in taper.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 39 days out and in taper—the mind games start here. Resist the urge to compensate for lower volume with intensity. Watch yesterday's 14-miler and moderate pace; that's your fitness snapshot. The next 5 weeks are about polishing sharpness and arriving fresh, not proving you can still go hard. Use today's easy run to visualize the descent sections in Kranjska Gora (where most 50K time is lost); mental rehearsal counts as training.
